title: Bekhorot 40
description: Blemishes that permit a firstborn animal to be slaughtered: the Temple's two cubit rods, testicles, extra legs, round hooves, dislocated hips, Ila's three blemishes at Yavne, jaws, doubled ears, tails, warts and eyes.
topics: 📏 The two cubit rods in the Shushan chamber, and why the Temple's craftsmen were paid by one and worked by the other
🔍 One testicle or two? Rabbi Yishmael's "it is known" against Rabbi Akiva's hands-on test, and the incident in Piran
🦵 Five legs, three legs, donkey hooves, the shaḥul and the kasul
🏛️ Ila lists the blemishes at Yavne and adds three the Sages had not heard of
👁️ A round eye like a person's: the contradiction from Niddah, settled by Rav Yosef
🐐 Jaws, doubled ears and a kid's tail; Rav Huna is refuted
🩹 A wart in the eye: bone or no bone, black or white, hair or no hair

a1.he: בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה, אַחַת עַל קֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית וְאַחַת עַל קֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית דְּרוֹמִית, שֶׁעַל קֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית הָיְתָה יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה חֲצִי אֶצְבַּע, וְשֶׁעַל קֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית דְּרוֹמִית הָיְתָה יְתֵירָה עָלֶיהָ חֲצִי אֶצְבַּע, נִמְצֵאת יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה אֶצְבַּע.

a2.he: וְלָמָה הָיוּ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה? (כשהיו) [שֶׁהָיוּ] אוּמָּנִין נוֹטְלִין בַּקְּטַנָּה, וּמַחְזִירִין בַּגְּדוֹלָה, שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹאוּ לִידֵי מְעִילָה.

a3.he: תַּרְתֵּי לְמָה לִי? חֲדָא — דְּכַסְפָּא וְזַהֲבָא, וַחֲדָא — דְּבִנְיָינָא.

a4.he: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, וְאִי תֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן, לְאוֹתָהּ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ: שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּשָׂר בֵּין חוּלְיָא לְחוּלְיָא מְלֹא אֶצְבַּע.

a5.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין לוֹ בֵּיצִים, אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי כִּיסִין — יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי בֵּיצִים, אֵין לוֹ שְׁנֵי כִּיסִין — אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מוֹשִׁיבוֹ עַל עַכּוּזוֹ וּמְמַעֵךְ, אִם יֵשׁ בֵּיצָה — סוֹפָהּ לָצֵאת. מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁמִּיעֵךְ וְלֹא יָצָא, נִשְׁחֲטָה וְנִמְצֵאת דְּבוּקָה בַּכְּסָלִים, וְהִתִּיר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְאָסַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי.

a6.he: גְּמָ׳ הַשְׁתָּא אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת אָמְרַתְּ הָוֵי מוּמָא, אֵין לוֹ כְּלָל מִיבַּעְיָא? חַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי: אֵין לוֹ שְׁתֵּי בֵּיצִים בִּשְׁתֵּי כִּיסִין אֶלָּא בְּכִיס אֶחָד, אִי נָמֵי שְׁתֵּי כִּיסִין וּבֵיצָה אַחַת — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם.

a7.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִּיסִים — בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי בֵּיצִים, אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא כִּיס אֶחָד — כְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת דָּמֵי, וַאֲתָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְמֵימַר: בְּיָדוּעַ לָא אָמְרִינַן, אֶלָּא מוֹשִׁיבוֹ עַל עַכּוּזוֹ וּמְמַעֵךְ, אִם יֵשׁ בֵּיצָה סוֹפוֹ לָצֵאת.

a8.he: וּמַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁמִּיעֵךְ וְלֹא יָצָא וְכוּ׳. תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּפָירָן שֶׁל בֵּית מְנַחֵם, שֶׁמִּיעֵךְ וְלֹא יָצָאת, וְנִשְׁחֲטָה וְנִמְצֵאת דְּבוּקָה בַּכְּסָלִים, וְהִתִּיר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וְאָסַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי.

a9.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי: עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מְכַלֶּה מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל! אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מַאֲכִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל נְבֵילוֹת! לָאו מִישְׁחָט שַׁחְטֵיהּ?

a10.he: אֶלָּא: טְרֵיפוֹת. לָא אִיסּוּר טְרֵיפוֹת הוּא?! אֶלָּא: עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מַאֲכִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל קָדָשִׁים בַּחוּץ!

a11.he: מַתְנִי׳ בַּעַל חָמֵשׁ רַגְלַיִם, אוֹ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא שָׁלֹשׁ, וְשֶׁרַגְלָיו קְלוּטוֹת כְּשֶׁל חֲמוֹר, וְהַשָּׁחוּל וְהַכָּסוּל. אֵיזֶהוּ שָׁחוּל? שֶׁנִּשְׁמְטָה יְרֵיכוֹ. וְכָסוּל? שֶׁאַחַת מִירֵיכוֹתָיו גְּבוֹהוֹת.

a12.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁחָסֵר וְיָתֵר בַּיָּד, אֲבָל בָּרֶגֶל — טְרֵפָה נָמֵי הָוֵי, דְּכֹל יָתֵיר כְּנָטוּל דָּמֵי.

a13.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא תֵּימָא דַּעֲגִילָן וְלָא סְדִיקָן, אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דַּעֲגִילָן, אַף עַל גַּב דִּסְדִיקָן.

a14.he: וְהַשָּׁחוּל וְהַכָּסוּל וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ כָּסוּל וְאֵיזֶהוּ שָׁחוּל? שָׁחוּל — שֶׁנִּשְׁמְטָה יְרֵיכוֹ, כָּסוּל — שֶׁרַגְלוֹ אֶחָד בְּתוֹךְ הַכֶּסֶל, וְרַגְלוֹ אֶחָד עַל גַּבֵּי הַכֶּסֶל. תָּנָא: הַשָּׂרוּעַ וְהַקָּלוּט — שָׂרוּעַ שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּרְבֵּב לוֹ יְרֵיכוֹ, קָלוּט — שֶׁרַגְלָיו קְלוּטוֹת כְּשֶׁל חֲמוֹר וּכְשֶׁל סוּס.

a15.he: מַתְנִי׳ נִשְׁבַּר עֶצֶם יָדוֹ וְעֶצֶם רַגְלוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר. מוּמִין אֵלּוּ מָנָה אִילָא בְּיַבְנֶה, וְהוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים.

a16.he: וְעוֹד שְׁלֹשָׁה הוֹסִיף, אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ. שֶׁגַּלְגַּל עֵינוֹ עָגוֹל כְּשֶׁל אָדָם, וּפִיו דּוֹמֶה כְּשֶׁל חֲזִיר, וְשֶׁנִּיטַּל רוֹב הַמְדַבֵּר בִּלְשׁוֹנוֹ. בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אַחֲרֵיהֶן אָמְרוּ: הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם.

a17.he: גְּמָ׳ אֵינוֹ נִיכָּר, מִי קָא הָוֵי מוּמָא? אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֵינוֹ נִיכָּר מֵחֲמַת עַצְמוֹ, אֲבָל נִיכָּר מֵחֲמַת מְלָאכָה.

a18.he: מוּמִין אֵלּוּ מָנָה וְכוּ׳. לְמֵימְרָא דְּלָאו הַיְינוּ אוֹרְחֵיהּ? וּרְמִינְהוּ: הַמַּפֶּלֶת מִין בְּהֵמָה וְחַיָּה וָעוֹף, בֵּין טְמֵאִין בֵּין טְהוֹרִין, אִם זָכָר תֵּשֵׁב לְזָכָר.

a19.he: אִם נְקֵבָה — תֵּשֵׁב לִנְקֵבָה, אֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ — תֵּשֵׁב לְזָכָר וְלִנְקֵבָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.

a20.he: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר? הוֹאִיל וְגַלְגַּל עֵינוֹ עָגוֹל כְּשֶׁל אָדָם! אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּאוּכָּמָא, הָא בְּחִיוָּורָא.

a21.he: וּפִיו דּוֹמֶה כְּשֶׁל חֲזִיר. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא תֵּימָא דִּשְׁפִיד וּפְרִוס, אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דִּפְרִוס אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא שְׁפִיד.

a22.he: וְשֶׁנִּיטַּל רוֹב הַמְדַבֵּר שֶׁבִּלְשׁוֹנוֹ. מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: וְאֶת שֶׁנִּיטַּל רוֹב הַלָּשׁוֹן, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: רוֹב הַמְדַבֵּר שֶׁל לְשׁוֹנוֹ.

a23.he: מַתְנִי׳ וּמַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהַלְּחִי הַתַּחְתּוֹן עוֹדֵף עַל הָעֶלְיוֹן, וְשָׁאַל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים, וְאָמְרוּ: הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם.

a24.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי תַּנָּא דְּקָתָנֵי ״וּמַעֲשֶׂה״? מִשּׁוּם דִּתְנַן ״פִּיו דּוֹמֶה לַחֲזִיר״, וּפְלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי, וְקָאָמְרִינַן: כִּי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי בִּשְׂפָתוֹ עֶלְיוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, אֲבָל שֶׁהַתַּחְתּוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם.

b1.he: וּמַעֲשֶׂה נָמֵי שֶׁלְּחִי הַתַּחְתּוֹן עוֹדֵף עַל הָעֶלְיוֹן, שָׁאַל רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים וְאָמְרוּ: הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם.

b2.he: וְהָא גַּבֵּי אָדָם הוּא דִּתְנַן: שְׂפָתוֹ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, אוֹ שֶׁתַּחְתּוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם. גַּבֵּי אָדָם הוּא דִּכְתִיב: ״אִישׁ אִישׁ מִזֶּרַע אַהֲרֹן״, אִישׁ שֶׁשָּׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן, אֲבָל בִּבְהֵמָה לָא!

b3.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאִית בַּהּ עֶצֶם, הָא דְּלֵית בַּהּ עֶצֶם.

b4.he: מַתְנִי׳ אוֹזֶן הַגְּדִי הָיְתָה כְּפוּלָה, אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא עֶצֶם אֶחָד — מוּם, בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ עֶצֶם — אֵינוֹ מוּם. רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: זְנַב הַגְּדִי שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֶה לְשֶׁל חֲזִיר, וְשֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שְׁלֹשׁ חוּלְיוֹת — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם.

b5.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פִּיו בָּלוּם וְרַגְלָיו מְבוּלָּמוֹת, מֵחֲמַת הָרוּחַ — אֵינוֹ מוּם, מֵחֲמַת הָעֶצֶם — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם. אׇזְנָיו כְּפוּלוֹת, בְּחַסְחֲסוּת אַחַת — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, בִּשְׁתֵּי חַסְחֲסֻיוֹת — אֵינוֹ מוּם.

b6.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: זְנַב הַגְּדִי שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֶה לְשֶׁל חֲזִיר. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא תֵּימָא דְּקַטִּינָא, אֶלָּא דִּכְרִיכָא, אַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲלִימָא.

b7.he: אוֹ שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שָׁלֹשׁ חוּלְיוֹת וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בַּגְּדִי — שְׁתַּיִם הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, שָׁלֹשׁ אֵינוֹ מוּם. בַּטָּלֶה — שָׁלֹשׁ הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, אַרְבַּע אֵינוֹ מוּם. מֵיתִיבִי: בַּגְּדִי — אַחַת הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, שְׁתַּיִם אֵינוֹ מוּם. בַּטָּלֶה — שְׁתַּיִם הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, שָׁלֹשׁ אֵינוֹ מוּם. תְּיוּבְתָּא דְרַב הוּנָא.

b8.he: וְרַב הוּנָא, מַתְנִיתִין אַטְעִיתֵיהּ; אִיהוּ סָבַר: מִדְּרֵישָׁא בִּגְדִי — סֵיפָא נָמֵי בִּגְדִי, וְלָא הִיא — רֵישָׁא בִּגְדִי, וְסֵיפָא בְּטָלֶה.

b9.he: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר: אֶת שֶׁיַּבֶּלֶת בְּעֵינָיו, וְשֶׁנִּפְגַּם עֶצֶם יָדוֹ וְרַגְלוֹ, וְשֶׁנִּפְרַק עַצְמוֹ שֶׁל פִּיו, עֵינוֹ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה, אׇזְנוֹ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה, בַּמַּרְאֶה אֲבָל לֹא בַּמִּדָּה. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּי בֵּיצָיו, אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה כִּשְׁתַּיִם שֶׁבַּחֲבֶירְתָּהּ, וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים.

b10.he: גְּמָ׳ לְמֵימְרָא דְּיַבֶּלֶת הָוֵי מוּמָא? וּרְמִינְהוּ: וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין עֲלֵיהֶן לֹא בְּמִקְדָּשׁ וְלֹא בַּמְּדִינָה — בַּעַל גָּרָב וּבַעַל יַבֶּלֶת!

b11.he: וְתִסְבְּרָא? הָא כְּתִיבָא ״יַבֶּלֶת״ בְּאוֹרָיְיתָא! אֶלָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — בְּגוּפוֹ, הָא — בְּעֵינוֹ.

b12.he: מִכְּדֵי קְרָא סְתָמָא, מָה לִי בְּגוּפוֹ וּמָה לִי בְּעֵינוֹ? אֶלָּא לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאִית בַּהּ עֶצֶם, הָא דְּלֵית בַּהּ עֶצֶם.

b13.he: דִּקְרָא — דְּאִית בַּהּ עֶצֶם, מַתְנִיתִין — דְּלֵית בַּהּ עֶצֶם; בְּעֵינוֹ — הָוֵי מוּמָא, בְּגוּפָא — לָא הָוֵי מוּמָא.

b14.he: וְלֵית לַהּ עֶצֶם בְּגוּפָא פְּסוּלָה? הֲרֵי תִּלְתּוּל בְּעָלְמָא הוּא, דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: בַּעֲלֵי הַתִּילּוּלִין פְּסוּלִין בָּאָדָם וּכְשֵׁירִין בַּבְּהֵמָה! אֶלָּא, אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּעֵינוֹ, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — בַּשָּׁחוֹר, הָא — בַּלָּבָן.

b15.he: וְהָא אֵין מוּמִין בַּלָּבָן! אֶלָּא: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בַּלָּבָן, וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא — דְּאִית בַּהּ שֵׂעָר, הָא — דְּלֵית בַּהּ שֵׂעָר.

b16.he: עֵינוֹ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְכוּ׳. תָּנָא: גְּדוֹלָה כְּשֶׁל עֵגֶל, קְטַנָּה כְּשֶׁל אַוָּוז.

b17.he: אׇזְנוֹ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְכוּ׳. וְרַבָּנַן עַד כַּמָּה? תַּנְיָא, אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: אֲפִילּוּ אֵינָהּ לַשְּׁנִיָּה אֶלָּא כְּפוֹל — כְּשֵׁירָה.

b18.he: מַתְנִי׳ זְנַב הָעֵגֶל — שֶׁאֵינָהּ מַגַּעַת לָעַרְקוֹב, אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: כֹּל מַרְבִּית עֲגָלִים כֵּן, כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיְּהוּ מְגַדְּלִין — הֵן נִמְתָּחוֹת. אֵיזֶהוּ עַרְקוֹב שֶׁאָמְרוּ? רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר: בְּעַרְקוֹב שֶׁבְּאֶמְצַע הַיָּרֵךְ.

messages.text: Continued from 39b. Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said the “fingerbreadth” the Sages spoke of is the one in this mishna about the Temple’s cubit rods (Kelim 17:9):

in the chamber of Shushan the capital, which was located above the eastern gate of the Temple Mount, one in the northeast corner and one in the southeast corner. The one that was in the northeast corner was longer than the cubit used by Moses in the building of the Tabernacle, which was six handbreadths, by half a fingerbreadth, and the one that was in the southeast corner was longer than the other one by another half a fingerbreadth. One therefore finds it longer than Moses’ cubit by a full fingerbreadth.
messages.lead: …There were two rods for measuring cubits

notes.he: יציע שעשוי על שער מזרח ומקרי שושן הבירה במנחות בפרק שתי הלחם (מנחות דף צח.):
notes.en: A gallery built over the eastern gate [of the Temple Mount], which was called Shushan the capital, as explained in Menachot, chapter Shtei HaLeḥem (98a).

notes.he: בש"א ד' אצבעות ולהכי קאמר כמה תהא משולשת דגדיל הוא שליש מן הענף והוי הענף ח' אצבעות וכולו ג' טפחים שהן זרת ומהכא ילפינן משך הציצית זרת דבמנחות לא ילפינן כמה ארכו. ואנן בציצית עבדינן כב"ש ד' חוטין וד' אצבעות גדיל:
notes.en: [On the tzitzit baraita of 39b:] Beit Shammai say four fingerbreadths. The braided part is a third of the strand, so the strand is eight fingerbreadths and the whole is three handbreadths, which is a span. From here we learn that tzitzit are a span long, since in Menachot we do not learn how long they are. And in tzitzit we practice like Beit Shammai: four strings and four fingerbreadths of braiding.

messages.caption: The three cubits: Moses’ cubit of six handbreadths, the northeast rod (+½ fingerbreadth) and the southeast rod (+1 fingerbreadth).

messages.text: And why did the Sages say that there should be two measures of a cubit, one large and one small? It was so that the artisans who were working in the Temple would take payment according the amount of work they did, as measured by the small cubit, and return it to the Temple through their work, as measured by the large cubit, so they would not come to misuse consecrated property. If they would accept any payment that they did not deserve, they would be misusing consecrated property.

notes.he: כשהיו מתנין עם האומנין לעשות כך וכך אמות מלאכה לבדק הבית היו מתנין בשל משה והן עושין למדה הגדולה למדת אחת שעושין בשושן הבירה:
notes.en: When they contracted with the craftsmen to do so many cubits of work for the Temple’s upkeep, they contracted by Moses’ cubit, and the craftsmen did the work by the larger measure, one of the cubits kept in Shushan the capital.

notes.he: שלא יהנו מן ההקדש דאם היו עושין באותה מדה שמתנין שמא יפחתו דא"א לצמצם הילכך מחזירין בגדולה:
notes.en: So that they would not benefit from consecrated property. Had they worked by the same measure they had contracted with, they might fall short, since it is impossible to be exact. So they “return” by the larger one.

messages.text: It was with regard to the fingerbreadth mentioned in this mishna that the baraita cited above teaches that it is one-fourth of a handbreadth of any average person.
messages.quote: longer than Moses’ cubit by a full fingerbreadth

notes.he: ורב הונא אמר אצבע שאמרו לענין אצבע דיתירה על של משה דהוי ד' בטפח של כל אדם:
notes.en: Rav Huna [son of Rav Yehoshua] says that the fingerbreadth the Sages spoke of is the fingerbreadth by which the cubit exceeds Moses’ cubit, which is a quarter of the handbreadth of any person.

messages.text: Why do I need two large cubits?

notes.he: בחד סגי (באותה) [לבד מאותה] של משה שהיא ו' טפחים:
notes.en: One would be enough, apart from Moses’ cubit of six handbreadths.

messages.text: One, the shorter of the two, was used to measure silver and gold. Since silver and gold were valuable, the difference between the two measurements was set at only half a fingerbreadth, so that the artisans would not suffer too great a loss. And the other one, which was longer than Moses’ cubit by a full fingerbreadth, was used in the construction of wood and stone structures.

notes.he: שמלאכת טורח היא מתנין בשל משה ומחזירין לאותה שגדולה הימנה חצי אצבע:
notes.en: Since that is painstaking work, they contracted by Moses’ cubit and delivered by the one that is larger than it by half a fingerbreadth.

notes.he: דחומה נוטלין בשל משה ומחזירין באותה שיתירה עליה אצבע:
notes.en: For building a wall, they were paid by Moses’ cubit and delivered by the one that exceeds it by a full fingerbreadth.

messages.alt: and some say Rav Huna bar Natan
messages.text: This baraita, which states that a fingerbreadth is one-fourth of a handbreadth of any average person, is referring to that which we learned in the mishna here with regard to the blemishes of a firstborn animal: In a case where there is a full fingerbreadth of flesh between one joint and another joint. That measure of a full fingerbreadth is one-fourth of a handbreadth.

notes.he: ורב נחמן אמר לאצבע דמתניתין דבין חוליא לחוליא:
notes.en: And Rav Naḥman says it refers to the fingerbreadth in our mishna, between one joint and the next.

messages.text: Mishna
The firstborn animal may be slaughtered if it has no testicles or if it has only one testicle.

notes.dh: מתני' אין לו ביצים או אין לו אלא ביצה אחת
notes.he: הוי מום:
notes.en: If it has no testicles, or has only one testicle, that is a blemish.

messages.text: If the animal has two scrotal sacs, it can be assumed that it has two testicles; if the animal does not have two scrotal sacs, it can be assumed that it has only one testicle.

notes.he: לכל בהמה יש לה לכל ביצה כיס אחת לפי שהכיס חלוק באמצעיתו ומבחוץ ניכר שהרי באמצע הוא משוקע ונראית בו שורה העמוקה:
notes.en: Every animal has a separate sac for each testicle: the scrotum is divided down the middle, and you can see it from outside, because the middle is sunken and a deep line shows there.

messages.text: The matter can be ascertained: One seats the animal on its rump and mashes the sac; if there is a testicle, ultimately it is going to emerge.

notes.he: גרסינן. והכי אמרינן בעירובין בפ' כיצד מעברין (עירובין דף נג:) אכוזו תנן או עכוזו תנן. על עכוזו על עגבותיו אחת מושיבין את הבכור שאין לו אלא ביצה אחת:
notes.en: We read akuzo, as discussed in Eruvin, chapter Keitzad Me’abrin (53b): did we learn akuzo or akuzo [with an alef or with an ayin]? “On its akuz” means on its haunches: one seats the firstborn that seems to have only one testicle on its hindquarters.

notes.he: וממשמש בכיס ובכסלים ואם יש סופה לצאת ואם אינה יוצאה הוי מום:
notes.en: He feels around the sac and the loins. If there is a testicle, it will eventually come out; if it does not come out, it is a blemish.

notes.he: פלנק"ש:
notes.en: Kesalim [loins]: in Old French, flancs, the flanks.

messages.text: There was an incident where one mashed the sac and the testicle did not emerge. Then, the animal was slaughtered and the testicle was discovered attached to the loins. And Rabbi Akiva permitted the consumption of its flesh, as the testicle had not previously emerged, and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri prohibited its consumption.

notes.he: דהוי מום הואיל ואינה במקומה:
notes.en: Rabbi Akiva permitted it: it counts as a blemish, since the testicle was not in its place.

notes.he: דכיון דנתמעך ולא יצא הוי מום ומותר לאוכלו:
notes.en: And Rabbi Akiva permitted it: since it was mashed and the testicle did not come out, it is a blemish, and it is permitted to eat it.

notes.he: ר' יוחנן בן נורי אסר הואיל ונמצאת:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri prohibited it, since the testicle was found.

messages.text: Gemara
Now that with regard to a case where it has only one testicle you said that it is a blemish, is it necessary to state the same in a case where it has no testicles at all?
messages.quote: it has no testicles or if it has only one testicle

messages.text: The mishna is incomplete and this is what it is teaching: If it does not have two testicles in two scrotal sacs, but in one sac, or alternatively, if it has two sacs and one testicle, it is a blemish.

notes.he: ור' ישמעאל אסיפא הוא דפליג דקאמר ת"ק אין לו אלא ביצה אחת בשני כיסין הוי מום ואתי רבי ישמעאל למימר בידוע שיש לו שתי ביצים אבל ארישא מודינא לך דכי אין לו אלא כיס אחד כמי שאין לו אלא ביצה אחת וכמעוך דמי:
notes.en: Rabbi Yishmael disputes only the latter clause. The first tanna says that one testicle with two sacs is a blemish, and Rabbi Yishmael comes to say that we know it has two testicles. But on the first clause he agrees: if it has only one sac, it is like one with only one testicle, and is treated like one whose testicles are crushed.

messages.text: The Gemara’s corrected version of the mishna continues:

If the animal has two scrotal sacs, it is known that it has two testicles, and therefore it is not blemished and may not be slaughtered; if the animal has only one scrotal sac it is considered like one that has only one testicle, even if it actually has two testicles.

notes.he: אין לו אלא כיס אחד אע"ג דיש לו ב' ביצים כמי שאין לו אלא ביצה אחת דמי ואתא ר' עקיבא וכו':
notes.en: If it has only one sac, even though it has two testicles, it is as though it has only one testicle. And Rabbi Akiva comes to say, etc.

messages.text: If it has two sacs, we do not say the claim of: It is known. Rather, one seats the animal on its rump and mashes the sac; if there is a testicle, ultimately it is going to emerge. If the testicle does not emerge, clearly it has only one testicle and is blemished.

notes.he: אע"ג דיש לו ב' כיסין בידוע שיש לו ב' ביצים והאחת טמונה בבטן אלא כך בודקו מושיבו לבכור על עכוזו ועל זנבו ועל עגבותיו וממעך בכיס ואם יש שם ביצה אחרת סופה לצאת:
notes.en: Rabbi Akiva says: even though it has two sacs, we do not say it is known that it has two testicles with the second hidden in the belly. Rather, this is how it is examined: one seats the firstborn on its rump, on its tail and haunches, and mashes the sac; if there is another testicle there, it will eventually come out.

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: And there was an incident where one mashed the sac and the testicle did not emerge.

messages.text: There was an incident in Piran of Beit Menaḥem where a firstborn animal apparently had only one testicle, and someone mashed its sac and the other testicle did not emerge. And the animal was slaughtered and the testicle was discovered attached to the loins. And Rabbi Akiva permitted its consumption, and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri prohibited its consumption.

notes.he: שם הכפר:
notes.en: Piran is the name of the village.

notes.he: פירש בקונטרס שם הכפר ובתוספתא (פ"ד) כתוב בפרה של בית מנחם כמו בההוא [מעשה בפרה של בית מנחם] שניטלה האם שלה (סנהדרין דף לג.):
notes.en: In Piran of Beit Menaḥem: Rashi explains that this is the name of the village. But the Tosefta (chapter 4) reads “with the cow [para] of Beit Menaḥem,” like the incident of the cow of Beit Menaḥem whose womb was removed (Sanhedrin 33a).

messages.text: @Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri Until when will you consume the property of the Jewish people by prohibiting animals in such cases?

notes.he: אתה מכלה ממונו של ישראל. דכיון שאתה אוסרן לאכול בחוץ אין לו תקנה אלא קבורה:
notes.en: “An incident with the cow of Beit Menaḥem.” You are destroying the property of Israel: since you forbid eating these animals outside the Temple, there is nothing to do with them but bury them.

messages.text: @Rabbi Akiva Until when will you feed the Jewish people unslaughtered animal carcasses?
messages.quote: Until when will you consume the property of the Jewish people

messages.text: How could Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri use the term animal carcasses here? After all, aren’t they properly slaughtered?
messages.quote: unslaughtered animal carcasses?

messages.text: Rather, Yoḥanan ben Nuri actually referred to animals with a wound that will cause them to die within twelve months [tereifot].

But it is not a prohibition of tereifot. Rather, he said: Until when will you feed the Jewish people sacrificial animals outside the Temple courtyard? According to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri this is not a blemish, and therefore the animal is an unblemished offering, which may not be eaten outside the Temple.

notes.he: שאין בו מום ובקדושתו הוא:
notes.en: Sacrificial animals outside: since it has no blemish, it is still in its sanctity.

notes.he: דתם הוי ואינו נאכל אלא בירושלם:
notes.en: Sacrificial animals outside: since it is unblemished, it may be eaten only in Jerusalem. (A later editor’s note: that is, in Temple times it would be eaten in Jerusalem and offered on the altar like any unblemished firstborn.)

messages.text: Mishna
An animal with five legs, or one that has only three, or one whose hooves on its legs were closed like those of a donkey and not split, or the shaḥul, or the kasul may be slaughtered.
What is a shaḥul? It is an animal with a thighbone that was dislocated. And what is a kasul? It is an animal whose build is asymmetrical in that one of its thighs is higher than the other.

notes.he: כגון דלא איעכל ניביה דאי איעכל ניביה טריפה נמי הוי כדאמרי' באלו טריפות (חולין דף נד:) האי בוקא דאטמא דשף מדוכתיה טריפה וה"מ דאיעכול ניביה:
notes.en: Whose thighbone was dislocated: where the sinew has not rotted. If the sinew had rotted it would also be a tereifa, as stated in Chullin, chapter Elu Tereifot (54b): if the hip-socket bone slipped from its place, it is a tereifa, and that applies when the sinew has rotted.

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס אישלויישי"ר בלע"ז וכגון דלא איעכול ניביה דאי איעכול ניביה טריפה נמי הוי כדאמר באלו טריפות (חולין דף נה:) האי בוקא דאטמא דשף מדוכתיה טריפה והני מילי דאיעכול ניביה וקשיא לפירושו דאיכא מאן דטריף התם אפילו לא איעכול ולא איפסוק אלא יש לפרש דנשמטה כן מתחלת ברייתה וכן נשתרבבה בסמוך:
notes.en: Whose thigh was dislocated: Rashi explains it (in Old French, esloisier, dislocated) as a case where the sinew had not rotted, for if it had, it would also be a tereifa, as stated in Chullin (55b). But this is difficult for his explanation, since there is an opinion there that it is a tereifa even if the sinew had not rotted or been severed. Rather, explain that it was dislocated this way from birth; and the same applies to “whose thigh is extended” below.

notes.he: מקום בוקא דאטמא של ירך זו עלה למעלה על הגב יותר מחבירתה:
notes.en: One higher than the other: the hip socket of this thigh has moved up toward the back, higher than the other one.

messages.text: Gemara

The Sages taught this only in a case where the animal was missing or had an additional foreleg. But if it was missing or had an additional hind leg, not only is it blemished, but it is also a tereifa. The reason is that any extra limb is like a removed limb, and an animal whose hind leg was removed is a tereifa.
messages.quote: An animal with five legs, or one that has only three

notes.he: דבעל ה' רגלים או שלשה דהוי מום ולא טריפה:
notes.en: They taught this only…: that an animal with five or three legs has a blemish and is not a tereifa.

notes.he: שהחיסור או הייתור הוו ביד שיש לו לבעל ה' רגלים ג' ידים וב' רגלים ולבעל ג' ב' רגלים ויד אחת דביד לא שייך טריפות:
notes.en: Only where what is missing or extra is a foreleg: the five-legged animal has three forelegs and two hind legs, and the three-legged one has two hind legs and one foreleg. The rules of tereifa do not apply to a foreleg.

notes.he: ובהמה שנטל ירך וחלל שלה נבילה וקי"ל בבהמה שנחתכו רגליה מן הארכובה ולמעלה טריפה ועוד בוקא דאטמא דשף מדוכתיה טריפה:
notes.en: It is like a removed limb: an animal whose thigh and its socket were removed is a neveila [carcass]. And we hold that an animal whose legs were cut off above the knee joint is a tereifa, and also that if the hip-socket bone slipped from its place it is a tereifa.

notes.he: דכל יתיר כנטול דמי ותנן בהמה שנחתכו רגליה מן הארכובה ולמעלה טרפה דשם ישנו לצומת הגידים:
notes.en: It is also a tereifa: since any extra limb is like a removed limb, and we learned that an animal whose legs were cut off from the knee joint upward is a tereifa, because that is where the sinews meet.

messages.text: Do not say that it is a blemish only in a case where its hooves are entirely like those of a donkey, i.e., round and not split at all. Rather, when they are round, even though they are also split, it is still considered a blemish.
messages.quote: whose hooves on its legs were closed like those of a donkey

notes.he: דמכל וכל דומות לחמור דעגילין ולא סדיקין:
notes.en: Do not say that they must resemble a donkey’s in every respect: round and not split.

notes.he: כשל חמור הוי מום דפרסות בהמה טהורה אינן עגולות:
notes.en: Rather, since they are round like a donkey’s, it is a blemish, because the hooves of a kosher animal are not round.

messages.text: In this regard, the Sages taught:
messages.quote: or the shaḥul, or the kasul

messages.text: What is the kasul and what is the shaḥul? The shaḥul is an animal with a thighbone that was dislocated. The kasul is an animal that is irregular in that one of its legs is inside the loin, i.e., in its proper place, and in one of its legs the bone is dislocated and is above the loin.

notes.he: פלנ"ק:
notes.en: Kesalei: in Old French, flanc, the flank.

notes.he: כך דרך הבהמה שהירך מחוברת באליה סמוך לכסלים ולא למעלה מן הכסלים דהיינו על גב האליה:
notes.en: Inside the loin: this is the normal build of the animal. The thigh joins the rump near the loins, not above them on the back of the rump.

notes.he: שרגלו אחת נכנסת בתוך הכסלים ורגלו אחת על גבי הכסל לסוף הכסל כדרכו:
notes.en: The kasul: one of its legs goes in among the loins, and its other leg sits on top of the loin, at the end of the loin.

messages.caption: A schematic, not an anatomy chart: a normal pair of thighbones, the shaḥul (dislocated) and the kasul (one thigh seated above the loin).

messages.text: What are the saru’a and kalut mentioned in the Torah among the animals disqualified from being sacrificed? The saru’a is one whose thigh is longer than the other; the kalut is one whose hooves on its legs are closed like those of a donkey and like those of a horse.

verse.he: וְשׁוֹר וָשֶׂה שָׂרוּעַ וְקָלוּט נְדָבָה תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתוֹ וּלְנֵדֶר לֹא יֵרָצֶה׃
verse.en: You may, however, present as a freewill offering an ox or a sheep with a limb extended or contracted; but it will not be accepted for a vow.

notes.he: שאחת מיריכותיו גדולה מחבירתה:
notes.en: Whose thigh is extended: one of its thighs is larger than the other.

notes.he: שארוכה מחברתה:
notes.en: Whose thigh is extended: it is longer than the other.

messages.text: Mishna
Additional blemishes that permit the slaughter of the firstborn include those where the bone of its foreleg or the bone of its hind leg was broken, even though it is not conspicuous.

notes.he: בגמרא מפרש:
notes.en: Even though it is not conspicuous: the Gemara explains this.

messages.text: With regard to these blemishes listed in this chapter, Ila, who was expert in blemishes of the firstborn, enumerated them in Yavne, and the Sages deferred to his expertise.
And Ila added three additional blemishes,
@Ila We did not hear about those.

notes.he: שהוזכרו למעלה. ואלו הן הג' שהוסיף את שגלגל עינו כו':
notes.en: We have heard only of these: the ones mentioned above. And these are the three he added: one whose eye is round, and so on.

messages.text: An animal whose eye is round like that of a person, or whose mouth is similar to that of a pig, or where most of the segment of its tongue corresponding to the segment that facilitates speech in the tongue of a person was removed.
messages.quote: We did not hear about those.

notes.he: מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: Like that of a pig: the Gemara explains this.

notes.he: היינו קצת הלשון שאינו דבוק במלקוחיו:
notes.en: Most of the speaking part: that is, the part of the tongue that is free and not attached to the jaw.

notes.he: רוב מן הלשון שנפרד מן החיך התחתון אותו שיכול לכפוף למעלה:
notes.en: Most of the speaking part of its tongue was removed: most of the part of the tongue that is free of the lower palate, the part it can bend upward.

messages.text: That is a blemish that enables the slaughter of the firstborn.
messages.lead: The court that followed them said with regard to each of those three blemishes:
messages.quote: whose eye is round like that of a person

messages.text: Gemara
If it is not conspicuous, is it a blemish? A blemish must be on an exposed part of the body (see 37b).
messages.quote: even though it is not conspicuous

notes.he: שאין השבר נראה אבל ניכר הוא מחמת שצולע והילוך הרגל זו היא מלאכתו:
notes.en: On its own account: the fracture itself cannot be seen, but you can tell because the animal limps. The walking of the leg is its “work.”

notes.he: אינו ניכר לחוץ מי הוי מומא מומין שבגלוי בעינן:
notes.en: It is not visible from outside, so is it a blemish? We require blemishes that are exposed.

messages.text: The mishna means that it is not conspicuous on its own account, i.e., the shape of the leg is no different from the usual. But it is conspicuous on account of its work, i.e., the manner in which the animal walks.

notes.he: שכשהולך נראה והליכה קרי מלאכה:
notes.en: But it is visible on account of its work: you can see it when it walks, and walking is called its work.

messages.text: Is this to say that it is not the manner of animals to have eyes of this kind? And one can raise a contradiction from a mishna:
messages.lead: The mishna teaches that with regard to these blemishes listed in this chapter, Ila enumerated them in Yavne, and he added three more, including an animal whose eye is round like that of a person.
messages.quote: whose eye is round like that of a person

notes.he: שיהא גלגל של בהמה עגול:
notes.en: That it is not its normal way: for an animal’s eye to be round.

notes.he: למיהוי עינו עגול כשל אדם:
notes.en: Is this to say that it is not its normal way for its eye to be round like a person’s?

messages.text: With regard to a woman who miscarries a fetus in the form of a type of domesticated animal, undomesticated animal, or bird, whether it is a non-kosher animal or whether it is a kosher animal, if it is male, the woman observes the periods of impurity, i.e., seven days, and purity, i.e., thirty-three days, established in the Torah for a woman who gives birth to a male.

notes.he: ימי טומאה שבעה ול"ג ימי טוהר:
notes.en: She observes for a male: seven days of impurity and thirty-three days of purity.

messages.text: If it is female, the woman observes the periods of impurity, i.e., fourteen days, and purity, i.e., sixty-six days, established in the Torah for a woman who gives birth to a female. If its sex is unknown, the woman observes the more severe restrictions from the case of the birth of a male and the more severe restrictions from the case of the birth of a female: She is impure for fourteen days like a woman who gave birth to a female, but blood that she sees thereafter is pure until only forty days after birth, like a woman who gave birth to a male. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: י"ד טמאים וס"ו טהורין:
notes.en: For a female: fourteen impure days and sixty-six pure ones.

notes.he: לחומרא ימי טומאה דנקיבה שבועיים וימי טוהר דזכר דלא יהא לה אלא ל"ג ימי טוהר:
notes.en: For a male and for a female, stringently: the days of impurity of a female, two weeks, and the days of purity of a male, so that she has only thirty-three days of purity.

notes.he: דמ' זכר ומיגווייהו נטרה י"ד ימי טומאה לנקבה:
notes.en: She observes for a male and for a female: forty days as for a male, and of the two she keeps fourteen days of impurity, as for a female.

messages.text: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir? Since the eye of these animals is round like that of a person, a woman who miscarries a fetus of this kind is impure.
messages.quote: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: דאמר היולדת מין בהמה טמאה לידה כולד מעליא:
notes.en: What is Rabbi Meir’s reason: for saying that a woman who gives birth to the form of a non-kosher animal has given birth, as with a real child.

notes.he: ודומה לאדם בגלגל העין:
notes.en: Since: it resembles a person in the eyeball.

messages.text: It is not difficult; this is referring to the black portion of the eye, whereas that is referring to the white portion of the eye.

notes.he: שחור של עין הבהמה (אינו) עגול כשל אדם:
notes.en: The black: the black of an animal’s eye is round like a person’s.

notes.he: כל בית מושב הלובן והסירא קרי ציריא והוא ודאי [אינו] עגול כשל אדם:
notes.en: The white: the whole setting of the white and the lid is called tzirya, and that is certainly not round like a person’s.

notes.he: כלומר אוכמא דעיניה אורחיה למיהוי עגול כשל אדם:
notes.en: This refers to the black and that to the white: that is, the black of the eye is normally round like a person’s.

notes.he: כלומר כוליה חריץ של עין לאו אורחיה:
notes.en: Tzirya: the whole opening of the eye. It is not normal for that to be round.

messages.text: Do not say that this is referring only to a case where the mouth is pointed and the upper lip overlaps the bottom lip, exactly like that of a pig. Rather, when it overlaps, even though it is not pointed, this is a blemish.
messages.quote: or its mouth is similar to that of a pig

notes.he: דבעי' דומה לחזיר מכל וכל דשפיד ופריס. שפיד פיו עגול פריס ששפה עליונה ולחיים העליונות עודפות על התחתונות. ומפי המורה איתמר לן איפכא דשפיד שלחייו העליונות הולכות ומתחדדות כשפוד:
notes.en: Do not say that it must resemble a pig in every respect, both shafid and paris. Shafid: its mouth is round. Paris: the upper lip and upper cheeks overhang the lower ones. But from my teacher we received the reverse: shafid means its upper cheeks narrow to a point, like a spit [shapud].

notes.he: חד כשל חזיר:
notes.en: Shafid: pointed, like a pig’s.

notes.he: ששפתו עקומה למעלה כחזיר:
notes.en: And paris: its lip curves upward like a pig’s.

messages.text: Whose opinion is expressed in the mishna?
messages.quote: or that most of its tongue … speech was removed

messages.text: It is the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught in a baraita:
Or that most of its tongue was removed;
Most of the segment of its tongue corresponding to the segment that facilitates speech in the tongue of a person must be removed to be considered a blemish.
Mishna
And there was an incident where the lower jaw of the firstborn protruded beyond the upper jaw, and Rabban Gamliel asked the Sages for a ruling,
That is a blemish that enables the slaughter of the firstborn.
Gemara
What is the ruling taught in the previous mishna that the tanna is referring to when he teaches here: And there was an incident?
messages.quote: And there was an incident

notes.he: דדמי להאי מעשה דקתני ומעשה:
notes.en: What did it teach: what is this incident like, that it says “and there was an incident”?

messages.text: Since we learned in the list of blemishes in the previous mishna the case where its mouth is similar to that of a pig, and the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Ila in that case, we say here that when the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Ila, it is only in a case where its upper lip overlaps the lower lip. But in a case where the lower jaw protrudes beyond the upper jaw, everyone agrees that this is a blemish.

notes.he: דאמרי לא שמענו את אלו:
notes.en: And the Rabbis disagree with him: since they said, “We did not hear about those.”

messages.text: The Gemara’s version of the mishna continues:
And there was also an incident where the lower jaw of the firstborn protruded beyond the upper jaw, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel asked the Sages for a ruling,
That is a blemish that enables the slaughter of the firstborn.
But it is with regard to the blemishes of a person that we learned in a mishna:
messages.quote: That is a blemish

notes.he: כהן:
notes.en: With regard to a person: that is, a kohen.

notes.he: שפתו העליונה עודפת כו':
notes.en: But we learned in the chapter below: “his upper lip protrudes,” etc.

messages.text: If his upper lip protrudes beyond the lower lip or his lower lip protrudes beyond the upper lip, that is a blemish.

And it is only with regard to a person that it is written: “Whatever man of the seed of Aaron” (Leviticus 22:4), which teaches that in order to be fit for the Temple service a priest must be a man who is equal to the seed of Aaron, i.e., he has an ordinary appearance like other priests. But this requirement is not stated with regard to an animal, and therefore an animal should not be considered blemished if its lower lip protrudes beyond the upper lip.

verse.he: אִישׁ אִישׁ מִזֶּרַע אַהֲרֹן וְהוּא צָרוּעַ אוֹ זָב בַּקֳּדָשִׁים לֹא יֹאכַל עַד אֲשֶׁר יִטְהָר וְהַנֹּגֵעַ בְּכׇל־טְמֵא־נֶפֶשׁ אוֹ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־תֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת־זָרַע׃
verse.en: No man whatsoever among Aaron’s offspring who has an eruption or a discharge shall eat of the sacred donations until he is pure. If one touches anything made impure by a corpse, or if a man has an emission of semen,

notes.he: אבל בבהמה לא הוי מומא:
notes.en: But in an animal it is not a blemish.

messages.text: That is not difficult; this mishna is referring to a case where the lower jaw contains a bone that is longer than the upper jaw, in which case it is a blemish even for an animal, whereas that mishna is referring to a case where the lower jaw does not contain a bone, and therefore it is a blemish only in the case of a person.

notes.he: אם עצם הלחי התחתון עודף על העליון הוי מום אפילו בבהמה אבל אין בה עצם אלא ששפתו התחתונה ארוכה ומקבלת העליונה ועודפת עליה באדם הוי מום ולא בבהמה:
notes.en: Where it contains a bone: if the lower jawbone protrudes beyond the upper one, it is a blemish even in an animal. But where there is no bone, only that the lower lip is long, takes in the upper lip and protrudes beyond it, that is a blemish in a person but not in an animal.

notes.he: דאית ביה עצם בשפתו התחתונה הוי מומא:
notes.en: It is not difficult: this is where there is a bone in its lower lip, and then it is a blemish.

messages.text: Mishna

With regard to the ear of the kid that was doubled and appeared like two ears, the Sages said: When the additional ear is one bone, i.e., it has its own cartilage, it is a blemish; when it does not have its own bone it is not a blemish.

notes.he: שיש לו שתי אזנים מצד אחד אוזן בתוך אוזן:
notes.en: The ear of the kid that was doubled: it has two ears on one side, an ear within an ear.

notes.he: שאין להם אלא תנוך אחד שנכפל תנוך העליון לתוכו ונתחבר למטה הרי זה מום:
notes.en: When it is one bone: they have only one cartilage. The upper cartilage folded into it and joined it below. That is a blemish.

notes.he: שהתנוכים מובדלים למעלה אינו מום. וטעמא לא איתפרש לי ולא דמי לבעלת ה' רגלים דהאי אוזן בתוך אוזן אינו נראה כל כך:
notes.en: When it does not have its own bone: the cartilages are separate at the top, and it is not a blemish. The reason was not explained to me, and it is not like an animal with five legs, because this ear within an ear is not so noticeable.

notes.he: בשנים:
notes.en: That was doubled: in two.

notes.he: שהסחוס שלה אחד ולמעלה נכפלת הוי מום:
notes.en: When it is one bone: it has one cartilage and is doubled above. That is a blemish.

messages.text: In the case of the tail of a kid that is similar to that of a pig or one that is so short that it does not have three joints, that is a blemish.

notes.he: מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: Like that of a pig: the Gemara explains this.

messages.text: Gemara
The Sages taught:

In a case where the mouth of a firstborn animal is swollen, and likewise, if its legs are swollen, the following distinction applies: If it is swollen due to the wind, i.e., it simply swelled up, it is not a blemish. If it is swollen due to a particularly large bone, this is a blemish.

notes.he: קצר:
notes.en: Balum: short.

notes.he: קצרות ברוחב אנקפלי"ד בלע"ז:
notes.en: Mevulamot: narrow in width. (Rashi adds an Old French gloss.)

notes.he: שאין לו ריוח כל כך בפה ולא בעצם ולא בבשר השפתים אינו מום:
notes.en: If due to the space: it simply lacks room in the mouth, neither in the bone nor in the flesh of the lips. That is not a blemish.

notes.he: שהשפתים פתוחות יפה אבל הלחיים אדוקות זו בזו שאינו יכול לפותחן דכי אכיל או פעי מרחיב השפתים ונראה העצם כנוד ה"ז מום. וכן ברגלים שרגליו קצרות מחמת הרוח של מדה אחת העצם והבשר של כפות הרגלים שלא היו רחבין כל כך אינו מום ואם מחמת העצם שהעצם קצר והבשר מרחיב מלמטה ויוצא לחוץ הרי זה מום. והמורה גריס מחמת הרוח ופירושה כדפרישנא אבל לתקן הלשון אין יכולת ואיכא דגרסי מחמת הריוח כדפרישנא. ל"א פיו בלום נפוח אם מחמת הרוח שנפח מחמת דיצא אינו מום דהדר בריא ואם מחמת העצם שעבה ביותר הרי זה מום ובתוספתא דבכורות (פ"ד ה"ד) מצאנו מחמת הרוח אינו מום מחמת עצמו ה"ז מום:
notes.en: If due to the bone: the lips open well, but the jaws are pressed together so that it cannot open them; when it eats or bleats it widens its lips, and the bone looks like a pouch. That is a blemish. The same for the legs: if they are short due to the space, because the bone and the flesh of the feet are of one measure and not very wide, it is not a blemish; if due to the bone, because the bone is short and the flesh widens below and sticks out, it is a blemish. My teacher read “due to the wind” and explained it as I did, but the wording cannot be corrected; others read “due to the space,” as I explained. Another explanation: “its mouth is balum” means swollen. If it swelled from a passing cause it is not a blemish, since it will heal; if due to the bone, which is very thick, it is a blemish. And in the Tosefta of Bekhorot (4:4) we found: due to the wind, it is not a blemish; due to itself, it is a blemish.

notes.he: פירש בקונטרס בלשון ב' נפוח וכו' בלשון ראשון שפי' ובלום קצר דבלום הוא לשון סתימה כמו חוטמו בלום דלקמן בפרק מומין אלו (בכורות דף מג:) דפירושו נקביו סתומין כדפי' לקמן בקונטרס וכמו בולם עצמו בשעת מריבה בפ' כיסוי הדם (חולין דף פט.):
notes.en: Its mouth is balum: Rashi gave, as a second explanation, “swollen.” His first explanation, that balum means short, is better, since balum is a word for closing up, as in “its nose is balum” below in chapter Mumin Elu (43b), which Rashi explains there as nostrils that are blocked; and as in “one who restrains [bolem] himself during a quarrel” in chapter Kisui HaDam (Chullin 89a).

notes.he: דחוק הרבה:
notes.en: Its mouth is balum: very narrow.

notes.he: חדות ודחוקו' הרבה הטלפיים:
notes.en: And its legs are mevulamot: the hooves are sharp and very tight.

notes.he: כלומר אם הוא בלום מחמת שאינו מרויחו אינו מום:
notes.en: If due to the space: that is, if it is narrow because it does not open it wide, it is not a blemish.

notes.he: שהעצם דחוק הרבה ומחמת כן אינו יכול לפתחו הוי מום:
notes.en: If narrow due to the bone: the bone is very tight and because of that it cannot open its mouth. That is a blemish.

messages.text: If its ears are doubled, in a case where it has one cartilage, this is a blemish; in a case where it has two cartilages, this is not a blemish.

notes.he: תנוך:
notes.en: Ḥasḥus: the cartilage of the ear.

notes.he: היינו סחוס:
notes.en: Ḥasḥus: that is, cartilage.

messages.text: The mishna teaches that Rabban Gamliel says: With regard to the tail of a kid that is similar to that of a pig, that is a blemish.
messages.quote: the tail of a kid that is similar to that of a pig

messages.text: Do not say that it is a blemish only where its tail is thin like that of a pig; rather, if it is round, i.e., curly like a pig’s tail, even though it is thick, like the tail of a goat, this is considered a blemish.
messages.quote: the tail of a kid that is similar to that of a pig

notes.he: דקה מאד:
notes.en: Ketina: very thin.

notes.he: עגולה שזנב הטלה הוי רחבה יתר על עוביה:
notes.en: Kerikha: round. A lamb’s tail is normally wider than it is thick.

notes.he: עגולה:
notes.en: Kerikha: round.

notes.he: רכה:
notes.en: Ketina: soft.

messages.text: In the case of the tail of a kid, if it has two joints, that is a blemish; if it has three joints, it is not a blemish. With regard to a lamb, if it has three joints, that is a blemish; if it has four joints, it is not a blemish.
messages.quote: Or that it does not have three joints

notes.he: חוליות בזנב ה"ז מום:
notes.en: In a kid, two: two joints in the tail is a blemish.

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita:

In the case of a kid, if its tail has one joint, that is a blemish; if it has two joints, it is not a blemish. With regard to a lamb, if it has two joints, that is a blemish; if it has three joints, it is not a blemish.
messages.quote: In the case of the tail of a kid, if it has two joints, that is a blemish

notes.he: שכן דרכה:
notes.en: Three is not a blemish, since that is its normal way.

messages.text: ✖ This is a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Rav Huna.

messages.caption: Tail joints: what Rav Huna said, and what the baraita that refutes him says.

messages.text: And Rav Huna issued his statement because the mishna misled him. He thought that from the fact that the first clause is referring to a kid, whose tail is similar to that of a pig, it can be inferred that the latter clause, with its mention of three joints, is also referring to a kid. But it is not so. Rather, the first clause is referring to a kid, but the latter clause is referring to a lamb, as explained in the baraita.

notes.he: אזן הגדי. סיפא אין בה שלש חוליות:
notes.en: The first clause is the ear of the kid. The latter clause is “that does not have three joints.”

notes.he: או שאין בה ג' חוליות בטלה קא מיירי:
notes.en: The latter clause, “or that it does not have three joints,” speaks of a lamb.

messages.text: Mishna

One that has a wart in its eyes; and one where the bone of its foreleg or hind leg was damaged; and one where the bone of its mouth, i.e., its jaw, was dislocated; and an animal with one of its eyes large and one small, or one of its ears large and one small where the difference in size is detectable by sight, but not if it is detectable only by being measured.

notes.he: ורואי"ן:
notes.en: Yabelet, a wart: in Old French, verrue.

notes.he: דניכר המום ולעיל איירי בנשבר:
notes.en: Where the bone of its foreleg was damaged: here the blemish is visible. Above (40a) it spoke of a bone that was broken.

notes.he: שהשיניים קבועות בו ולמעלה מן החוטין דאי חוטין גופיה אפילו נפגמו או נגממו נמי:
notes.en: The bone of its mouth: the bone in which the teeth are set, above the gums. If it were the gums themselves, even a damaged or worn-down gum would also be a blemish.

notes.he: שלכל נראה שזו גדולה מזו:
notes.en: By sight: anyone can see that this one is larger than that one.

notes.he: שאם אין ניכר אלא במדה אינו מום:
notes.en: But not by measurement: if it can be noticed only by measuring, it is not a blemish.

notes.he: לחיו:
notes.en: Or the bone of its mouth was damaged: its jaw.

messages.text: An animal is blemished if with regard to its two testicles, one is as large as two of the other,
but the Rabbis did not agree with his opinion.

notes.he: ארבי יהודה קאי:
notes.en: But the Rabbis did not agree with him: this refers to Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: Gemara
Is this to say that a wart is considered a blemish? And one can raise a contradiction from the mishna:
messages.quote: One that has a wart in its eyes

messages.text: And these are the blemishes that one does not slaughter the firstborn due to them, neither in the Temple nor in the rest of the country, as these are not considered full-fledged blemishes… an animal with boils that are moist inside and out, and one with warts.

notes.he: דנפסל מן המזבח:
notes.en: Not in the Temple: since it is disqualified from the altar.

notes.he: דאינו מום גמור לישחט עליו בחוץ:
notes.en: Nor in the country: since it is not a full blemish that would allow it to be slaughtered outside.

notes.he: חזזית:
notes.en: Garav: a scabby skin eruption.

notes.he: הבכור במקדש להקריבו דשמא מום הוא:
notes.en: That one does not slaughter on account of them: one may not slaughter the firstborn in the Temple to offer it, because perhaps it is a blemish.

notes.he: דשמא לא הוי מומא ואסור לשוחטו במדינה אלא על מום גמור:
notes.en: Nor in the country: because perhaps it is not a blemish, and outside one may slaughter it only on account of a definite blemish.

notes.he: אלמא דלא הוי מום גמור:
notes.en: And one with a wart: this shows that it is not a full blemish.

messages.text: And how can you understand that a wart is not a blemish? After all, a wart is written in the Torah in its list of blemishes.

verse.he: עַוֶּרֶת אוֹ שָׁבוּר אוֹ־חָרוּץ אוֹ־יַבֶּלֶת אוֹ גָרָב אוֹ יַלֶּפֶת לֹא־תַקְרִיבוּ אֵלֶּה לַיהֹוָה וְאִשֶּׁה לֹא־תִתְּנוּ מֵהֶם עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Anything blind, or injured, or maimed, or with a wen, boil-scar, or scurvy—such you shall not offer to GOD; you shall not put any of them on the altar as offerings by fire to GOD.

notes.he: דלא מום הוא:
notes.en: And how can you understand it: that it is not a blemish?

notes.he: גבי מומין גמורין (ויקרא כב) עורת או שבור או חרוץ או יבלת:
notes.en: But a wart is written in the Torah: among the full blemishes (Leviticus 22): “blind, or broken, or maimed, or with a wart.”

messages.text: Rather, it is not difficult, as that mishna, which states that a wart is not a full-fledged blemish, is referring to a blemish on the animal’s body, whereas this mention of a wart in the Torah and the mishna here is referring to a wart in its eye.

notes.he: לא מום גמור הוא:
notes.en: On its body: there it is not a full blemish.

messages.text: Now consider that the verse is written in an unspecified manner. What difference is it to me if the wart is on its body, and what difference is it to me if the wart is in its eye? How is this distinction derived from the verse?

notes.he: כתיב:
notes.en: But the verse is written without qualification.

messages.text: Rather, it is not difficult, as this is referring to a wart that has a bone, and that is referring to a wart that does not have a bone.

notes.he: בגופו נמי הוי מום ולא קשיא קרא דמשמע דאפילו בגופו הוי מום אמתני' דמשמע דאינו מום גמור אלא בעין אבל בגופו מום הוא ליפסל ולא לישחט קרא דאית ביה עצם ומתני' הכא דבעין הוי מום ואידך מתני' דבגופו לא הוי מום בדלית בה עצם:
notes.en: Rather: on the body too it is a blemish. The verse, which implies a wart on the body is a blemish, does not contradict the mishna, which implies that it is a full blemish only in the eye while on the body it disqualifies from the altar but does not permit slaughter outside. The verse speaks of a wart that has a bone; our mishna here, in the eye, is a blemish; and the other mishna, on the body, is not a blemish because it has no bone.

messages.text: The wart mentioned in the verse and the mishna here is one that has a bone, whereas the wart addressed by the mishna there is one that does not have a bone. Consequently, if the wart is in its eye, it is a blemish, as stated in the verse and the mishna here, but if it is on its body, it is not a blemish, although the animal is disqualified from being sacrificed, in accordance with the ruling of the mishna there.

notes.he: דקתני אין שוחטין על יבלת היינו כי הויא בגופו ומתניתין וקרא דחשיב ליה מום כי הויא בעינו דקרא אית ביה עצם ביבלת שבגופו הוי מום. ומתניתין דאין שוחטין דלית ביה עצם הא בעינו אע"ג דלית בה עצם הוי מומא. בגופו לא הוי מום. כי לית בה עצם הא פסול הוי להקרבה. אמאי תלתול בעלמא. תלתול כעין שומא של בשר שתולה בעור:
notes.en: It is not difficult: the mishna that says one does not slaughter on account of a wart is when it is on the body; the mishna and the verse that count it as a blemish are when it is in the eye. The verse speaks of a wart that has a bone, and a wart on the body with a bone is a blemish. The mishna that says one does not slaughter speaks of one without a bone. In the eye, even without a bone it is a blemish; on the body without a bone it is not a blemish. “But it is disqualified from being offered? Why? It is mere hanging flesh.” Taltul is like a mole of flesh hanging from the skin.

messages.text: And with regard to a wart that does not have a bone and is on the body, is the animal disqualified from being sacrificed? It is merely hanging flesh, as we learned in a mishna:

notes.dh: ולית ביה עצם בגופו פסולה הוי
notes.he: בתמיה:
notes.en: And where it has no bone, on the body, it is disqualified? This is asked in surprise.

notes.he: חתיכות בשר התלויים בו כגון בני אדם שיש להם אצל אזניהם רצועות קטנות של בשר וממעי אמן הם:
notes.en: Taltul: pieces of flesh that hang from the body, like people who have small strips of flesh beside their ears from birth.

messages.text: With regard to those with flesh or skin that hangs from their body, such a blemish disqualifies a person, but with regard to such an animal, it is fit.

notes.he: אם כהן הוא פסול לעבודה דבעינן שוה בזרעו של אהרן:
notes.en: Disqualifies a person: if he is a kohen, he is disqualified from the Temple service, since we require one who is “equal to the seed of Aaron.”

messages.text: Rather, both this mishna here and that mishna there are referring to a wart in the animal’s eye, and it is not difficult, as this mishna is referring to a wart in the black of the eye, the pupil, whereas that mishna is referring to a wart in the white of the eye.

notes.he: אמתני' קאי ולא אקרא:
notes.en: Rather, both refer to the eye: this refers to the two mishnayot, not to the verse.

messages.text: But it has been established that there are no blemishes in the white part of the eye, which indicates that the animal is not even disqualified from being sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: ואפילו במקדש כשר לשחוט:
notes.en: But there are no blemishes in the white: so even in the Temple it may be slaughtered as an offering.

notes.he: ואע"ג דפלוגתא היא לעיל (בכורות דף לח:) הא אוקימנא לעיל מתני' כמ"ד אין מומין בלבן:
notes.en: But there are no blemishes in the white: although that is disputed above (38b), we already established the mishna there according to the view that there are no blemishes in the white.

notes.he: אין מומין בלבן אמאי אין שוחטין במקדש:
notes.en: The white: there are no blemishes in the white, so why may one not slaughter it in the Temple?

messages.text: Rather, both this statement that there are no blemishes in the white of the eye and that ruling of the mishna that a wart disqualifies the animal from being sacrificed are referring to a wart in the white part of the eye.

notes.he: הא דקתני אין שוחטין במקדש ובמדינה בלבן והא נמי דקתני אין מומין בלבן תרוייהו ליבלת במומין שבלבן אית ביה שער מגונה הוא ועלה קתני מתני' אין שוחטין לא במקדש ולא במדינה:
notes.en: Both: the mishna that says one does not slaughter in the Temple or in the country, and the teaching that there are no blemishes in the white, both speak of a wart in the white. Where it has a hair it is unsightly, and about that the mishna says one slaughters neither in the Temple nor in the country.

notes.he: ולא גרסינן בלבן:
notes.en: Rather, both refer to the black: that is our reading; we do not read “the white.”

notes.he: (ליש' בכלה כך דרשו בשבתא דריגלא):
notes.en: Rather, both refer to the white. (This is how it was expounded at the kallah, on the Shabbat before the festival.)

messages.text: It is not difficult; this is referring to a wart that has a hair, and therefore the animal is unfit for the altar, whereas that statement is referring to a case where the wart does not have a hair.

notes.he: דקתני אין מומין בלבן בדלית בה שער ומתני' דמום גמור הוא כדאוקימנא בשחור ובדלית נמי עצם וקרא בדאית בה עצם דאי מתניתין דהכא בדאית בה עצם אמאי נקט בעינו:
notes.en: And that: the teaching “there are no blemishes in the white” is where the wart has no hair. And our mishna, that it is a full blemish, is in the black, as we established, and also where it has no bone; the verse is where it has a bone. For if our mishna here were where it has a bone, why would it specify “in its eye”?

notes.he: ביבלת שהלבן הוי מומא והא קמ"ל אע"ג דשאר מום לא פסול בלבן אי אית ביה שיער פסיל ואי ליכא שיער בו לא פסיל:
notes.en: This, where it has a hair: a wart in the white is a blemish. It teaches that although other blemishes in the white do not disqualify, if the wart has a hair it disqualifies, and if it has no hair it does not.

messages.text: As for the mishna here, which rules that a wart is a full-fledged blemish, it is referring to a wart in the pupil of the eye, as explained.
In this regard, it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: one of its eyes large and one small

messages.text: When the mishna states the term large, it means the eye is as large as the eye of a calf, and when it states the term small, it means it is as small as that of a goose.
And according to the Rabbis, how large can the difference between the two testicles be without this discrepancy being considered a blemish?
messages.lead: The mishna teaches: Or one of its ears is large and one is small… and Rabbi Yehuda’s ruling, with which the Rabbis did not agree.
messages.quote: its two testicles, one is as large as two of the other

notes.he: דלא הודו לו בביצים עד כמה תהא חבירתה קטנה דמכשרי:
notes.en: And the Rabbis, who did not agree with him about the testicles: how much smaller may the other one be and still be fit, in their view?

notes.he: כלומר דלא יהיב שיעורא לאוזן גדולה כי היכי דיהיב לעין גדולה ולביצה גדולה:
notes.en: By sight but not by measurement: that is, it gives no measure for a large ear the way it gives one for a large eye and a large testicle.

notes.he: דלא הודו לו עד כמה תהא האחת קטנה מחברתה דהוי מומא עד פחות מכפול:
notes.en: And the Rabbis, who did not agree with him: how much smaller than the other may one testicle be before it is a blemish, if double is not enough?

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita:
Even if the second, smaller testicle is no bigger than a bean, the animal is fit.
Mishna

In the case of the tail of a calf that does not reach the leg joint [la’arkov], the Sages said: It is a blemish, because all growth of calves is in this manner: As long as they grow, their tails are extended beneath the leg joint.

notes.he: לפרק שבירך ובגמ' מפרש איזה ערקוב:
notes.en: La’arkov: to the joint of the thigh. The Gemara explains which joint.

notes.he: כל תרבות מנהג של עגלים כך הוא שיש זנבן מגיעות לערקוב הילכך בציר מהני הוי מומא וכשהן גדולים הולכות ונמתחות עד למטה:
notes.en: All growth of calves: the whole development and normal way of calves is that their tails reach that joint, so anything shorter is a blemish. As they grow, the tails keep stretching further down.

notes.he: מקום כף הירך:
notes.en: Arkov: the place of the hip socket.

messages.text: Which is the leg joint about which the Sages spoke?
They are referring to the leg joint that is in the middle of the thigh.
messages.quote: Which is the leg joint about which the Sages spoke?

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: In the middle of the thigh: the Gemara explains this.

messages.text: Continues on 41a: the Gemara explains which joint is meant.
